# What zr supports

zr compiles a Ruby program only when the binary gives exactly
what ruby 4.0.7 gives ([the contract](../explanation/the-contract.md)).
Where it cannot promise that, it refuses the program with exit
status 3 and names the form and its line. This page lists what
zr refuses, as the compiler itself lists it. Other differences
from ruby, all on purpose, are in
[Differences from ruby](differences-from-ruby.md), and what each
target can do is in [Targets](targets.md).

## Syntax that zr refuses

The compiler refuses these forms by name. Any other syntax node
that it does not know is refused with the node's name, for
example `interpolated xstring (InterpolatedXString)`.

- A block in an index target
- A dynamic constant path
- Redo outside a block or loop
- Retry outside a rescue clause
- `BEGIN { }` outside the toplevel
- `break` or `next` outside a block or loop

## Libraries that a program cannot require

A `require` of one of these names compiles, and raises
`LoadError` with the reason when it runs, so a guarded
require that never runs costs nothing. Every other library of
ruby 4.0.7 is there: the default and bundled gems, and ruby's
own `lib/`. A program cannot require a gem that ruby does not
ship (see [Use a library or gem](../how-to/use-a-library-or-gem.md)).

### `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-linux-musl`, `wasm32-wasi`

- `date_core`
- `mkmf`, which writes a C extension's Makefile: zr compiles no C
- `portable_ruby_gems`
- `prism/ffi`, the FFI half of prism: this runtime's prism is a Ruby port of the C
- `prism/lex_ripper`
- `prism/translation/parser`
- `prism/translation/parser/builder`
- `prism/translation/parser/compiler`
- `prism/translation/parser/lexer`
- `prism/translation/parser_current`
- `prism/translation/parser_versions`
- `prism/translation/ripper/shim`
- `prism/translation/ruby_parser`
- `ractor`
- `strscan/strscan`
- 61 encoding libraries under `enc/`: ruby loads them itself, and zr's runtime has every encoding built in

## Tests that a target may fail

Each target other than `aarch64-apple-darwin` has a baseline: the
end-to-end programs and spec examples that it may fail, each with
the reason. A test in a baseline that passes fails the run, so
these lists are current.

### aarch64-linux-musl

None.
